text: Our curve is f of x equals x cubed over three, minus x.
caption: Our curve is f(x) = x cubed over 3, minus x

text: It climbs to a hill, falls into a valley, then climbs again.
Start at x equals minus two, on the far left of the curve.
The tangent line here shows how steep the curve is at this point.
Its slope is three, so the curve climbs steeply here.
Underneath, a second graph will record the slope at every x.
A dashed line joins the same x on both graphs.
Slope three becomes a dot at height three on the lower graph.
caption: Slope 3 becomes a dot at height 3 on the lower graph

text: Now slide the point right, and the dot draws a trail below.
At the hilltop, x equals minus one, the tangent is perfectly flat.
Flat means slope zero, so the dot sits right on the axis.
The top of the hill lines up exactly with a zero below.
Keep sliding right, going downhill now, toward x equals zero.
Downhill slopes are negative, so the dot has dropped below the axis.
At x equals zero, the slope has fallen to minus one.
Slide on toward x equals one, where the valley bottoms out.
At the valley floor the tangent is flat again, slope zero.
So the bottom of the valley also lines up with a zero.
Now climb out of the valley, all the way to x equals two.
Uphill again, so the slope is positive, back up at three.
The trail of dots is a whole new curve: the slope graph.
This slope graph is the derivative, x squared minus one.
At x equals one, one squared minus one is zero, as we saw.
Wherever f climbs, the slope graph sits above the axis.
Wherever f falls, the slope graph dips below the axis.
And wherever f turns around, the slope graph crosses zero.
So a derivative is not just one number, it is a whole function.
Read the slope graph, and you know where the curve rises and falls.
